newsitem.title: POLAND: NO DECISION ON POLISH C.BANK DEPOSIT COLLECTION.
newsitem.headline: NO DECISION ON POLISH C.BANK DEPOSIT COLLECTION.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland is examining the possibility of accepting deposits from the public, but no decisions to open up such accounts have been made so far, an NBP spokesman said on Tuesday.

"We are at the stage of evaluating such a possibility, but the final decision will depend on the reaction of commercial banks (to the central bank's official interest rate increase," Krzysztof Mielnicki told Reuters.
The NBP increased its lombard rate by two points to 27 percent and its discount rate by 2.5 points to 24.5 percent on August 4.
On Tuesday the Gazeta Wyborcza daily quoted unofficial sources as saying that from the start of September the central bank would open term deposit accounts for individual citizens but not for firms.
Gazeta said that interest on the deposits was not yet set, but that they would be one to two points higher than comparable rates in commercial banks.

Earlier this month central bank president Hanna Gronkiewicz -Waltz said that the central bank would collect deposits from the public, to offset the inflationary effect of large flood relief credit for the government, when it was ready to do so.
"To guard against the lowering of deposit rates among banks in response to the central bank rate rise, the NBP will also start collecting six- and nine-month deposits," she has said.
